ESPN Streaming Plan Price Increase Effective in September 2026

 Aug 24, 2026 8:46am PT 

# ESPN to Hike Prices of Streaming Plans Next Month 

 By Todd Spangler 

 

 ESPN 

 ESPN is ratcheting up the price of its streaming services — just in time for the busy fall sports season.

 Effective Sept. 17, the Disney-owned sports giant is increasing the monthly and annual pricing for both ESPN Unlimited and the scaled-down ESPN Select tier.

 The price of ESPN Unlimited is increasing from $29.99 to $31.99/month. The cost of the annual ESPN Unlimited plan is rising from $299.99 to $319.99/year. In addition to everything on the ESPN and ESPN2 linear networks, the stand-alone sports package includes ESPNU, ESPNews, ESPN Deportes, SECN, SECN+, ACCN, and ACCNX plus thousands of additional live sporting events per year. 

 All told, ESPN Unlimited offers more than 47,000 live events each year, including every major sport and championship ESPN presents. The streaming service also recently integrated NFL Network and CW Sports on the ESPN App, and includes features like the personalized “SportsCenter For You”; Verts vertical video; and StreamCenter, a synchronized two-screen experience connecting mobile and connected TV devices. 

 ESPN Select is going from $12.99 to $13.99/month, while the annual plan is increasing from $129.99 to $139.99/year. ESPN Select provides some 32,000 live events annually but does not include access to the ESPN linear networks.

 In an Aug. 20 memo to ESPN staffers reviewed by Variety, chairman Jimmy Pitaro praised the team that launched the stand-alone streaming service a year ago.

 Disney has not disclosed how many subscribers have signed up for the ESPN streaming plans. 

 “From the beginning, we set out to provide sports fans with optionality and a new way to connect with ESPN. Early on, we have delivered,” Pitaro wrote. “To everyone across ESPN and Disney who continues to work tirelessly to build this platform — thank you. While we’re still in the early innings of our direct-to-consumer journey, one year after the launch of ESPN DTC, we move forward with absolute confidence in where we are headed.” 

 “We’re heading into the fall in an exceptionally strong position,” Pitaro wrote in the memo. “The NFL preseason has begun, and we are truly excited about the entire season leading to our first Super Bowl. College football will also kick off soon, a new LaLiga season is already underway, U.S. Open tennis begins this weekend, and so much more lies ahead. Our rights portfolio has never been stronger, and we have strong momentum.”

 According to Pitaro, “maximizing access” the ESPN streaming services has been a priority, “and that focus has led to meaningful progress this year. In fact, subscribers across nearly every major pay TV provider — including recent additions Comcast Xfinity and YouTube TV — can unlock the full ESPN Unlimited tier experience on the ESPN App at no additional cost. We are also focused on supporting Disney+ by unlocking additional content for its subscribers, in service of our One Disney initiative.”

# ESPN Unlimited Plan Explained: What’s Included & How To Get It

by Explore Disney+ Contributor

June 23, 2026

See how much it costs, how it compares to the ESPN Select plan, bundle options, and how to subscribe

Choosing a streaming plan should be easier than keeping up with your favorite teams. The ESPN Unlimited Plan gives fans access to ESPN’s full lineup of networks and services, whether the day calls for a marquee matchup, a studio show, or a documentary about one of sports’ biggest moments.

Before you pick a plan, here’s a quick rundown on who the ESPN Unlimited plan is best for, how it compares with other ESPN options, and what to know if you’re deciding between Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN bundle plans.

## What is the ESPN Unlimited Plan?

The ESPN Unlimited plan is a streaming subscription that gives fans access to the full ESPN lineup. That includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra, ESPN+, and now NFL Network.

It’s made for fans who want live games, ESPN studio shows, documentaries, replays, and more in one place, especially those without a traditional TV package.

## What’s included with the ESPN Unlimited plan?

With the ESPN Unlimited plan, you can stream all of ESPN’s live linear networks, NFL Network, and ESPN+, SECN+, and ACCNX content through a single subscription. That means access to thousands of live events, studio shows like SportsCenter, on-demand programming, ESPN Originals, and the 30 for 30 library.

Availability can vary by event, location, and league rules, so it’s a good idea to check the ESPN app before game time.

## How much does the ESPN Unlimited plan cost?

The subscription is available for $29.99 per month or $299.99 per year.

## How does ESPN Unlimited compare to ESPN Select?

ESPN Select gives you access to ESPN+ content. ESPN Unlimited builds on ESPN Select by adding live access to all of ESPN’s networks and services.

So, if you want ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network, ACC Network, NFL Network, ESPN+, and more under one subscription, ESPN Unlimited is the plan for you.

## Can I bundle the ESPN Unlimited plan with Disney+ and Hulu?

Yes. You can get the ESPN Unlimited plan as part of the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle, starting at $35.99 per month.

That means you can combine the ESPN Unlimited plan with Disney+ and Hulu in one subscription, making it the perfect option for households with sports fans, movie watchers, and TV lovers.*

## How can you get the ESPN Unlimited plan?

You can get the ESPN Unlimited plan with a Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle. Once your subscription is active, open the ESPN hub on Disney+ to browse sports, teams, leagues, and tournaments.

You can also subscribe to the ESPN Unlimited plan through the ESPN app. Create an account or log in with your MyDisney account and choose the ESPN Unlimited plan.

## ESPN Unlimited Imposing First Price Hike, Effective Sept. 17

Erik Gruenwedel

August 23, 2026

ESPN Unlimited, the all-inclusive subscription streaming service for all ESPN content, is set to impose its first price increase since launching on Aug. 21, 2025. The hike is effective Sept. 17.

The Disney-owned platform is raising standalone subscriptions for both ESPN Unlimited and ESPN Select (formerly ESPN+) $2 to $31.99 monthly, and $1 to $13.99 monthly, respectively. The annual prices increase $20 ($319.99) and $10 ($139.99), respectively.

The $36 monthly subscription fee for the ESPN Unlimited, ad-supported Disney+ and ad-supported Hulu bundle reportedly remains unchanged. The bundle reportedly comprises around 80% of all ESPN Unlimited subs.

 The bundle combining Disney+, Hulu, and the lower-tier ESPN Select is increasing from $20 to $22 per month (or $30 to $33 per month for the ad-free version), according to ESPN’s support page. 

No pricing updates have been announced for discounted add-on options, including Fox One and NFL+ Premium.

Disney has never publicly disclosed subscriber data for ESPN Unlimited.

# How to stream ESPN without cable in 2026

Pictured: The Kingdom. Image via TMDB.

Cutting the cord used to mean giving up live sports. Not anymore. ESPN now sells its channels and its streaming content directly to you, no cable subscription required, and the choice comes down to two plans with two very different jobs.

This guide breaks down ESPN streaming the honest way. What ESPN Select actually carries, what ESPN Unlimited adds, what each costs as of September 26, 2026, the devices that run the app, and the bundles where ESPN Unlimited already comes attached to something you might buy anyway. By the end you will know exactly which plan matches how you watch.

## The two ESPN plans, explained

ESPN sells two plans direct, and the names tell you less than the contents do. ESPN Select is $13.99 monthly or $139.99 a year, as of September 26, 2026. This is the plan built entirely from ESPN+ content. Top-tier soccer, PGA TOUR, NHL, college sports and a selection of other ESPN programming. If you remember ESPN+, this is where that content lives now.

One thing Select does not do is carry the ESPN cable channel itself. The networks’ live broadcasts and studio shows like SportsCenter sit in Unlimited, not here. Select is for the streaming-first sports fan who wants soccer, golf and college coverage without paying for the full channel lineup.

ESPN Unlimited is the bigger swing at $31.99 monthly or $319.99 a year, as of September 26, 2026. It includes all of the ESPN networks plus ESPN+: ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPN on ABC, SEC Network+, ACC Network Extra, NFL Network and CW Sports.

If you signed up before August 20, 2026, ESPN says you keep your old price until your first billing date after September 17, 2026. Worth checking your account if you are a longtime subscriber before you assume the new numbers apply to you.

## What ESPN Unlimited actually carries

This is the plan that replaces cable for most sports households. ESPN lists NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, tennis and golf majors, WWE, and SEC, ACC and Big 12 football and basketball. The studio shows are here too: SportsCenter, First Take and College GameDay.

Postseason is where Unlimited earns its price. ESPN lists postseason coverage from the NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB and the College Football Playoff. That is a full calendar of live sports, not a highlights service.

One caveat matters if you activate through a TV provider rather than buying direct. ESPN notes that when Unlimited is activated through a provider, content the provider does not carry may be missing. Buying direct from ESPN avoids that gap.

## The devices that run ESPN

ESPN's app is nearly everywhere. Per ESPN's supported devices page, it runs on Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV (4th generation and later), Chromecast, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox and Android TV, plus smart TVs from Hisense, LG webOS, Samsung Tizen and Vizio SmartCast, along with Xumo TV and the XiOne Box.

It also reaches into existing provider hardware: Xfinity Flex and X1 boxes and Cox Contour. On the go, the ESPN app covers iPhone and iPad, Android phones and tablets, Amazon Fire tablets, Windows 10 and 11 computers, and any modern web browser.

In short, if you own a recent smart TV or one of the mainstream streaming devices above, you can watch. There is no special box to buy just for ESPN.

## Where ESPN Unlimited comes bundled

You do not always have to buy ESPN on its own. Per Disney's bundle page, read September 26, 2026, the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle is $35.99 monthly, pairing Disney+ with ads, Hulu with ads and ESPN Unlimited with ads. The Premium version is $44.99 monthly, which drops the ads on Disney+ and Hulu while keeping ESPN Unlimited with ads.

ESPN is raising prices on Unlimited and Select plans — here's how to avoid the increase or get the service for free

## There are some ways to keep streaming everything on ESPN Unlimited at no extra cost.

Danica Creahan, Liz Kocan

Thu, September 17, 2026 at 7:57 PM UTC

View larger image

Here's how to save a few bucks and avoid the new ESPN price increases. (Choreograph (Konstantin Yuganov) via Getty Images)

ESPN Unlimited is ESPN's premium streaming tier, which launched in 2025. Initially, the service cost subscribers $29.99/month (or $299.99/year) for access to all of ESPN's linear networks, including ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SECN, ACCN, ESPNews and ESPN Deportes, plus access to programming on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX. A less-expensive option, ESPN Select, which is essentially a more robust version of the old ESPN+, also launched, costing $12.99/month.

But as is customary with all streaming services, those initial rates weren't going to last forever, and this week, ESPN announced that its Unlimited plan price has increased to $31.99/month, or $319.99/year, and the Select plan is now $13.99/month, or $139.99/year.

While we do love the fact that an ESPN Unlimited plan provides access to thousands of live events and other original programming, all of these increases take a toll on the old wallet. Fortunately, there are a few ways to make things hurt a little less. ESPN Unlimited is actually included in the price of several live TV streaming services like Fubo and DirecTV, cable providers like Spectrum, or you can bundle it with other platforms like FOX One to save big on monthly fees.

Here are some of the best ways to avoid ESPN's new price increases or get the plan for free!

DIRECTV offers several packages at all different price tiers, but if you want to get ESPN Unlimited included in one of them, you'll need to sign up for either their Choice, Ultimate or Premier packages (see all the plan descriptions and offerings here). Prices start at $64.99/month for your first month, and you'll also get unlimited Cloud DVR storage and access to Disney+, Hulu (with ads) included in each of these plans.

If you're a sports fanatic with little use for news or entertainment channels, DIRECTV's MySports Genre Pack costs even less, just $44.99 for your first 6 months, and it includes ESPN Unlimited along with 20+ additional sports channels. You can also try out any plan for free for five days.

### Save with a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundle

### Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited 

We're fans of the Disney+/Hulu/ESPN Unlimited bundle; even though it's pricey at $35.99/month, it's a must-have for its vast array of sports and entertainment offerings, and even though ESPN just raised their subscription rates, the cost of the bundle hasn't increased.

(Football fans, take note: You can also add a subscription to NFL+ Premium to the bundle and pay $45.99/month. That's a $5/month savings, considering that a standalone NFL+ Premium subscription costs $14.99/month. A subscription to NFL+ Premium gets you live local & primetime regular season and postseason games on your phone or tablet, access to the NFL Network, live out-of-market preseason games, live game audio for every game, plus NFL Red Zone, NFL Pro, and full game replays.)

### Save with an ESPN Unlimited/FOX One bundle

ESPN Unlimited rolls all 7 ESPN-affiliated networks — ESPN, ESPN2, SEC Network, ACC Network, along with ESPN+, SEC+ and ACCNX — into one plan. It's effectively "cable ESPN, but via streaming." # What is the new ESPN DTC service? Plans, costs, key facts

ESPN

- ESPN

Aug 21, 2026, 12:30 AM

ESPN launched a direct-to-consumer service in August 2025. The service offers major enhancements within ESPN's streaming and app experiences. Here are key facts to know:

New streaming plan details

When did ESPN direct-to-consumer launch?

The service brought the full suite of ESPN networks and services directly to fans in August 2025.

How can I subscribe to ESPN direct-to-consumer?

Fans can sign up for the new service here.

What plans does ESPN direct-to-consumer offer?

Fans can choose from two plans:

ESPN Unlimited Plan

- Access to all of ESPN's linear networks -- ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes, SEC Network, ACC Network -- in addition to ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+ and ACCNX
- 47,000 live events a year, on demand replays, studio shows, original programming and more

ESPN Select Plan

- Access to all content available on ESPN+
- More than 32,000 live sports events annually, a robust library of exclusive studio shows, on-demand replays, acclaimed original content and more

How much does each plan cost?

ESPN Unlimited Plan: $31.99 a month or $319.99 a year

ESPN Select Plan: $13.99 a month or $139.99 a year

What is available only on the ESPN Unlimited Plan vs. the ESPN Select Plan?

ESPN Unlimited Plan subscribers have access to all ESPN networks, including ESPN+, with events like NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, tennis and golf majors, top-tier college football and basketball, WWE and postseason coverage from all those and more.

ESPN Select Plan subscribers have access only to ESPN+, with top-tier soccer, PGA Tour, NHL, UFC and a selection of college sports, tennis, PLL, UFL and other leagues.

Do you get access to ESPN Unlimited as part of your pay-TV package?

Customers with Hulu + Live TV, DIRECTV, Fubo TV, Spectrum TV, Verizon FiOS, U-verse, Cox, Comcast Xfinity, and other supported providers may already get ESPN Unlimited as part of their pay-TV package, with more partners to come. To activate your ESPN plan or to learn more, please visit the ESPN Fan Support Activation FAQ.

Do both plans include advertising?

Like linear television, both plans have ads during live events and studio shows. Bundle options with Disney+ and Hulu will be available with or without ads on those platforms.

New app plan details

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact the overall ESPN app experience?

The enhanced ESPN app integrates game stats, betting information, fantasy sports, commerce, multiview options and a personalized SportsCenter For You. The new features and functionality are available to all fans who watch sports on the ESPN App, whether they subscribe directly or through pay-TV.

If I already use the existing ESPN App, do I need to download anything else with ESPN direct-to-consumer?

All features are available within the existing ESPN App on mobile devices and connected TV.

Impact of ESPN direct-to-consumer on existing plans

If I am an ESPN+ subscriber, do I still have access to the same content?

ESPN+ will continue to be available in a variety of ways. Existing ESPN+ subscribers will become subscribers to the ESPN Select Plan.

How does ESPN direct-to-consumer impact existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers?

Existing Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ bundle subscribers will become subscribers to a Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+ Select bundle and continue to receive the same content through the ESPN and Disney+ apps.

ESPN will continue to be distributed via pay-TV providers. Pay TV subscribers will have access to the enhanced features within the ESPN App via their pay-TV subscriptions.

# ESPN’s streaming app now costs $13.99 a month for Select and $31.99 for Unlimited

 By Tyler Foster 

 Published September 28, 2026 

 Image Credit: AirportExpert - CC0/Wiki Commons 

A monthly ESPN Select subscription now costs $13.99, and ESPN Unlimited costs $31.99, according to ESPN’s own pricing page, up from $12.99 and $29.99. The stand-alone app, sold as a way to watch live sports without a cable package, rolled out this increase on a subscriber-by-subscriber timeline tied to when someone originally signed up, a different mechanic than the single companywide date Disney applied to Disney+ and Hulu the same month.

What a rising ESPN bill doesn’t cover: The Senior Property Tax & Home-Cost Relief Kit offers an application log and renewal calendar for the property-tax side of the same household budget. Log renewal dates for property-tax relief programs →

## Two tiers, one app, two different dollar jumps

ESPN Select rose from $12.99 to $13.99 a month, or from $129.99 to $139.99 a year, while ESPN Unlimited rose from $29.99 to $31.99 a month, or from $299.99 to $319.99 a year, according to ESPN’s own plans-and-pricing support page. In dollar terms, Unlimited’s two-dollar monthly increase is twice the one-dollar increase applied to Select, even though the two moves work out to roughly similar percentage jumps, about eight percent for Select and about seven percent for Unlimited.

On an annual basis the same ratio holds: Select’s yearly price rose from $129.99 to $139.99, a ten-dollar jump, while Unlimited’s yearly price rose from $299.99 to $319.99, a twenty-dollar jump, exactly double Select’s increase in both the monthly and annual figures. That consistency, Select always moving by half of what Unlimited moves, points to both tiers being priced off the same underlying formula rather than adjusted independently of each other.

Both figures match what Sports Media Watch reported when the change was first announced, and the outlet noted these are the first price increases ESPN has applied to Select and Unlimited since the direct-to-consumer app launched in 2025. A year without a price change, followed by one increase across both tiers at once, is a different rhythm than the smaller, more frequent increments Disney has used on the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu tiers.

ESPN Select and Unlimited are sold as stand-alone subscriptions, watched through the ESPN app rather than bundled into a cable package, positioning them as an alternative for a household that has already dropped traditional pay television. The new prices apply to that direct subscription regardless of whether a household also carries a Disney+ or Hulu subscription through some other arrangement.

## A grandfather date instead of a single rollout day

ESPN’s own support page describes a mechanic tied to two specific dates rather than a single companywide rollout: anyone who subscribed before August 20, 2026 keeps the old $12.99 or $29.99 price until their first billing date after September 17, 2026. That creates a window of nearly a month, from August 20 to September 17, during which the exact price a subscriber pays depends on precisely when they signed up.

That two-date structure differs from how Disney rolled out its own Disney+ and Hulu price changes the same month, where new subscribers paid the higher price immediately and existing subscribers moved up on their very next bill, with no multi-week grandfather period described in that coverage. ESPN’s approach effectively gave subscribers who joined just before August 20 close to a full extra month at the old rate before the new one took hold.

Because monthly billing dates are spread across every day of the month depending on when a subscriber first signed up, “first billing date after September 17” is not one single day for the entire subscriber base. Someone billed on the 18th of each month saw the new

New Direct-to-Consumer Offering to be Singularly Branded ESPN - ESPN Press Room U.S.

- ESPN linear networks available direct to fans for first time ever in early fall

- Enhanced ESPN App to introduce new features, personalized fan-friendly experiences

Recognizing the deep connection the ESPN brand has established with sports fans and the significance of the moment, the new direct-to-consumer (DTC) streaming service will be named ESPN, it was announced today by Jimmy Pitaro, ESPN Chairman. Fans will have two ESPN DTC plans from which to choose, including an unlimited package that delivers the entire suite of ESPN networks and content.

Designed to give fans more choice, flexibility and access to all of ESPN via the enhanced ESPN App, the plans will cost $29.99/month for the unlimited package and $11.99/month for a select option. There will also be bundling opportunities for the ESPN unlimited plan with Disney+ and Hulu, including a special offer at launch for $29.99/month for the first 12 months. It was previously announced that the direct-to-consumer offering will launch in early fall and that ESPN will continue to be available through traditional MVPDs and DMVPDs.

“We are providing everything ESPN has to offer directly to fans and all in one place,” Pitaro said. “As we thought about the name, we kept returning to the fact that, across every generation, ESPN is the most trusted, loved and recognized name in sports, and that we should keep it simple and double down on the power of ESPN. Our straightforward approach to name and pricing will help fans cut through the clutter, and provide them compelling options to access all our content within the enhanced ESPN App. It will be the ultimate sports destination for personalized experiences and features, and, on top of that, fans will be able to choose to bundle ESPN with the industry-leading Disney+ and Hulu streaming services.”

The unlimited plan will give fans access to all of ESPN’s linear networks – ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SECN, ACCN, ESPNEWS, ESPN Deportes – in addition to ESPN on ABC, ESPN+, ESPN3, SECN+, and ACCNX, covering 47,000 live events each year, on-demand replays, studio shows, original programming, and more. ESPN’s unprecedented rights portfolio includes the NFL; NBA; NHL; MLB; WNBA; UFC; UFL; SEC; ACC; Big 12; College Football Playoff; 40 NCAA championships including the NCAA Women’s Basketball Championship; LaLiga, Bundesliga, NWSL, and FA Cup soccer; Australian Open, Wimbledon and US Open tennis; The Masters, PGA Championship, PGA TOUR, and TGL golf; Little League World Series baseball and softball; Premier Lacrosse League; and more. ESPN’s leading studio shows include the iconic SportsCenter, Get Up, First Take, NFL Live, The Pat McAfee Show, Pardon the Interruption, College GameDay, NBA Today, and others, along with on-demand content including 30 for 30 films, ESPN Originals, and more.

- Special offer at launch: Disney+, Hulu, ESPN unlimited bundle for $29.99/month for the first 12 months (with ads on Disney+/Hulu)

The select plan will provide subscribers with access to all content available on ESPN+, including more than 32,000 live sports events annually, a robust library of exclusive studio shows, on-demand replays, acclaimed original content, and more.
